comment: THE CLAUDE CODE VERSION FLOOR — the harness's enforcement layer IS `.claude/settings.json` plus hooks, which makes Claude Code its most load-bearing dependency and the only one whose own security history it never consulted. Through 0.5.0 this file did not exist: the harness held every framework it ships to a cited floor (tools/framework-floor.json) and held the tool it RUNS INSIDE to nothing. THE CITATIONS ARE THE POINT, not the number. A bare `"floor": "2.1.163"` is a number the next maintainer lowers when a teammate's CLI is old, because nothing in the file says what it costs; a floor whose every digit is attached to a published advisory is a number nobody lowers by accident. `advisories` is a SNAPSHOT of `gh api /advisories?ecosystem=npm&affects=@anthropic-ai/claude-code`, taken on `checkedOn`, reduced to the advisories that set the floor plus every one that lands on this harness's own surface — it is evidence, not a vulnerability database, and the gate re-derives the floor FROM it rather than trusting the scalar. TWO GATES READ THIS FILE, SPLIT ON THE CLOCK, and no third one exists: the CLOCKLESS arithmetic (does the scalar equal the evidence beside it?) rides `version-sync` in the chain, because `pnpm validate` must give the same verdict on the same tree forever; the CLOCKFUL question (has anyone re-queried lately?) rides the scheduled `floor-review` job, where a lapsed review blocks a maintainer rather than a contributor. SOURCE: design/CONTROL-PLANE-FACTS.md (Fact 10)

required.why: The earliest release outside EVERY published vulnerable range: the maximum `first_patched_version` across all 28 npm-scoped advisories. Derived, not chosen — `version-sync` recomputes it from `surfaceAdvisories` below and reds if this scalar drifts from the evidence in either direction.

recommended.why: `sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` — the setting that makes a non-allowlisted host FAIL rather than prompt. Recommended rather than required because the sandbox is opt-in in this harness (see docs/security/sandbox-and-supply-chain.md) and requiring 56 releases beyond the security evidence would be a floor the evidence does not support. A floor that overreaches is a floor people route around.

featureFloors.feature: `last_assistant_message` on Stop/SubagentStop — the field .claude/hooks/subagent-verdict.mjs reads. Below this the reviewer-verdict ledger cannot be written without scraping a transcript.

`CLAUDE_CODE_STOP_HOOK_BLOCK_CAP` and the 8-consecutive-block cap. Below this a red Stop hook loops forever instead of ending the turn with a warning — .harness/turn-outcomes.jsonl records the cap, and there is no cap to record.
`hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext` on Stop/SubagentStop. Not used today; noted because it lands on the same version the security floor already requires.
`sandbox.network.strictAllowlist` (user/managed/CLI settings only — ignored from project settings).

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Sandbox escape via persistent configuration injection in settings.json
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: `.claude/settings.json` is not a config file to this harness — it IS the enforcement layer, wiring every hook. An injection into it is an injection into the control plane.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Workspace trust dialog bypass via a repo-controlled settings file
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: The scaffold ships a settings file into every consumer repo. The trust dialog is what stands between cloning a repo and running its hooks.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Command injection via piped `sed` bypasses file-write restrictions
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: This repo's own doctrine says the bash guard is a TRIPWIRE, not a sandbox, and that obfuscated commands evade substring checks. These two are that caveat as SHIPPED CVEs rather than as a disclaimer — which is the argument for the floor, not against the guard.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Command injection via directory change bypasses write protection
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: pretool-write-guard.mjs judges PATHS. A bypass via directory change is a bypass of the thing it judges.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Sandbox escape via symlink following allows arbitrary file write outside the workspace
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: The write-guard already resolves links out of the project tree (a canary covers it); this is the same class one layer down, in the tool itself.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Insecure system-wide configuration loading enables local privilege escalation on Windows
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: Windows is the platform where this harness is thinnest — no sandbox support, and no Bash tool at all without Git Bash. A Windows-specific config-loading privesc lands exactly there.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Trust dialog bypass via git worktree spoofing allows arbitrary code execution
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: One of TWO worktree escapes. Worktree isolation is a natural recommendation for read-only reviewer subagents; these two are why that recommendation carries a version floor rather than standing alone.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Sandbox escape via git worktree path confusion allows unsandboxed code execution
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: The second worktree escape, and one of the two advisories that SET the required floor.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Out-of-band data exfiltration via a pre-approved domain in WebFetch
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: The other advisory that sets the floor — and a direct argument against treating a domain allowlist as an exfiltration control, which is how docs/security/sandbox-and-supply-chain.md must describe it.

surfaceAdvisories.summary: Insecure temporary file in the /copy command enables response disclosure and symlink-based file write
surfaceAdvisories.whyItMattersHere: The newest advisory in the set. Included because 'newest' and 'sets the floor' are different properties, and conflating them is how a floor gets lowered.

uncvedHookFixes.what: A PreToolUse hook returning "allow" could bypass `permissions.deny` rules, including enterprise managed settings.
`permissions.deny` did not override a PreToolUse hook's `permissionDecision: "ask"` — the hook could downgrade a deny into a prompt.
`PermissionRequest` hooks returning `updatedInput` were not re-checked against `permissions.deny`.

uncvedHookFixes.note: None of these three carries a CVE, so no advisory query finds them — and every one is a hook-versus-permission interaction, which is precisely this harness's enforcement model. They sit BELOW the required floor, so the floor already covers them; they are recorded because the next person to compute a floor should know that the advisory database alone would have missed them.

notNpmScoped.why: Appears on the anthropics/claude-code repository advisory page but is scoped to the `anthropic` ecosystem, not npm. It cannot set an npm floor.

notNpmScoped.product: Claude Desktop (SSH remote development, not Windows-specific)
notNpmScoped.why: Same: repository advisory page, `anthropic` ecosystem, returns 404 from /advisories/<ghsa>.

howToRefresh: Re-run `advisorySource`, update `checkedOn`, `advisoryCount`, and any advisory whose `first_patched_version` exceeds the current `required.version`. Then re-run `node tools/check-version-sync.mjs`, which recomputes the floor from `surfaceAdvisories` and reds if the scalar disagrees. RAISING the floor is routine. LOWERING it is not: every digit below is attached to a published advisory, so a lower number means a consumer running a version with a known escape in the tool that enforces everything else.
